Individual trajectories across visits (spaghetti plot)

Source: R/plot-visits.R
plot_trajectories.Rd

plot_trajectories() draws one thin line per subject, a thick summary line (median or mean) per group and, optionally, boxplots per visit. plot_trajectory_grid() draws one panel per root.

Usage

plot_trajectories(
  data,
  vars,
  id_col,
  group = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  time_labels = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  y_lab = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  show_box = TRUE,
  summary_fun = c("median", "mean"),
  line_alpha = 0.25,
  base_size = 11,
  ref_line = NULL
)

plot_trajectory_grid(
  data,
  roots,
  id_col,
  visits = c("V0", "V3"),
  group = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  ncol = 3,
  base_size = 10,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Wide format (one column per visit).

vars

Columns in chronological order, e.g. c(NFL_V0, NFL_V3) (names or tidyselect).

id_col

Subject identifier.

group

Optional colour variable.

labels

Optional named vector of labels.

time_labels

Visit labels (default: the suffixes of vars).

title, y_lab

Title (default: label of the root) and y-axis title.

palette

Colours of the groups.

show_box

Boxplots per visit (and group) in the background.

summary_fun

"median" or "mean".

line_alpha

Transparency of the subject lines.

base_size

Base font size.

ref_line

Optional horizontal reference line.

roots

Root names (one panel each).

visits

Visit suffixes.

ncol

Number of columns of panels.

...

Passed to plot_trajectories().

Value

A ggplot (NULL when fewer than 3 complete subjects), or a patchwork for plot_trajectory_grid().

Examples

plot_trajectories(cohort_sim, c(MOCA_V0, MOCA_V3), id_col = ID, group = GROUP)

plot_trajectory_grid(cohort_sim, c("NFL", "MOCA", "UPDRS"), id_col = "ID", group = "GROUP")
